Notes on Slow Reading

I have been trying to read more slowly this year. Not less, but more slowly: one chapter in an evening rather than four, with a pencil in my hand and time to stop at a sentence I like and read it again aloud.

A pencil helps. So does putting the phone in another room, which sounds obvious, but I resisted it for months before I tried it properly.

What changed

The first thing I noticed was that I remembered more. Not facts so much as the shape of an argument, and the voice of the writer, which stayed with me through the next day in a way it never did when I raced.

Small habits

  • One chapter, then stop, even when the next one calls.
  • Write a line in the margin about what surprised me.
A deeper note

Reading slowly is not the same as reading carefully, but the one leads to the other more often than not, and that is enough of a reason for me to keep at it through the winter.
